requirements.evidence: app/Ops/DiscordOpsAlert.php:30-52 does a no-op for null/'' (`! is_string($url) || $url === ''`), POSTs `['content' => ...]` with `Http::timeout(5)->asJson()`, and logs `Log::error('Discord ops alert failed', ['status' => ...])` for non-2xx and a scrubbed message when the transport throws; format() at :57-66 builds title/message/`key=value` lines and calls `mb_substr(..., 0, 1800)`; redact() at :72-85 covers sensitive keys (`api[_-]?key`, webhook, case-insensitive), Bearer values and recursion, with nested arrays sent through json_encode in stringify(). config/logging.php:57 defaults to 'daily' and :76-82 adds the audit channel (daily, audit.log, level info, days 90); no discord channel. config/services.php adds services.discord.webhook_url. .env.example and phpunit.xml set LOG_STACK=daily. docs/ops/logging.md is added. The existing daily channel is not in the diff, but LoggingConfigTest asserts days 14.

conventions.evidence: Tests are Pest tests (tests/Feature/Ops/DiscordOpsAlertTest.php, tests/Feature/LoggingConfigTest.php). CHANGELOG.md gets Added/Changed entries under [Unreleased]. docs/ops/logging.md is the doc that conventions.md already links to. PHPDoc is on send(). The task explicitly asks for a plain service class, so this is not a forbidden service layer. Style is Pint-compatible (`new DiscordOpsAlert`, `$key.'='`).

security.evidence: The webhook URL is never logged: only the status is logged for non-2xx (:46), and scrub() (:100-105) strips the exact URL and any `/api/webhooks/` URL from exception messages. Redaction checks keys before recursing, so a sensitive key that holds an array is fully redacted. Bearer tokens are redacted under any key. No user-facing input surface.

tests.evidence: DiscordOpsAlertTest covers the no-op for null and '' (assertNothingSent), the exact URL/method/JSON/content, an exact 1800 multibyte length, every redaction rule including nested JSON, non-2xx logging without the token, and transport-exception scrubbing. LoggingConfigTest checks the daily/audit/stack/no-discord config. Weak spot: 'the audit channel accepts writes' only asserts `Log::channel('audit')` is not null (tests/Feature/LoggingConfigTest.php:22-26), and it writes a real file under storage during the test.

simplicity.evidence: One ~100-line class with small private helpers (format/redact/stringify/scrub) and constants for the limits and regexes. It reuses Laravel's HTTP client and the Log facade. There are no extra abstractions, interfaces or bindings.

readability.evidence: Clear constant names (MAX_LENGTH, SENSITIVE_KEY, BEARER_VALUE), a short class docblock explaining the 'never throws, no URL in logs' contract, and a readable `match (true)` in stringify(). There is no dead code.

scope.evidence: Every file touched (.env.example, CHANGELOG.md, the new class, config/logging.php, config/services.php, docs/ops/logging.md, phpunit.xml, two tests) serves the task. The notifier is not wired into jobs or handlers, as the out-of-scope section requires.

issues.explanation: The audit-write test asserts only that the channel object is not null. It never checks that the entry was written (or that info-level passes and debug is filtered), and it writes to the real storage/logs directory.
`env('LOG_AUDIT_DAYS', 90)` returns a string when the env key is set. Monolog accepts it, but casting to int would keep the config type stable for strict comparisons.

A global `const DISCORD_TEST_URL` and a global helper function `sentContent()` in a Pest file can collide with other test files later. sentContent() would also raise a TypeError instead of a clear assertion failure if nothing was sent.

review.summary: The change adds App\Ops\DiscordOpsAlert with config-driven no-op behaviour, multibyte truncation, recursive and Bearer redaction, and soft-fail error logging that scrubs the webhook URL. It also adds the audit daily channel, switches the stack to daily, and documents the three lanes with CHANGELOG and .env.example updates. Requirements and contract are fully met with focused tests. The only gaps are a weak audit-write test and small test-hygiene nits, so I would approve with nits.
